headline: Highest risk is medium: no shared I/O or network paths are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors are largely blocked; only compliance uncertainty remains from docs-only evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent documents a shared communication channel, clipboard, MCP, filesystem, or stdin/stdout bridge. Agent A has no io_surfaces listed, and agent B explicitly has clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, and MCP all false. With no documented path for A’s outputs to reach B as instructions, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected through a shared clipboard, file drop, or MCP bridge, reassess upward.
IF A begins emitting content that B parses from a shared channel, injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared clipboard and file mounts.
Do not route A’s text into B without a sanitizer.
Document any future bridge before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No shared workspace, file access, or network egress is documented for either agent. Agent A has network_egress none, and agent B has read_filesystem and write_filesystem false with no files listed. Because neither profile shows a path for sensitive data to move from one agent to the other or out to a third party, leakage is not supported by the evidence.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or shared OAuth principal is introduced, reassess.
IF either agent is given file-reading or upload capability, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid mounting sensitive directories into either agent.
Verify no hidden upload path is added in orchestration.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles show no overlapping write authority: agent A exposes no filesystem or git permissions, and agent B explicitly cannot write files or modify git state. Without shared mutable resources or locking concerns, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair.
conditions: IF A is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as B, reassess.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, conflict risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for B.
Do not co-locate both agents on the same mutable repo.
Use separate sandboxes if write access is added later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is not documented as taking actions based on A’s outputs, and B lacks external action surfaces such as shell, browser, subprocess, or network egress. A is a game-playing agent with no documented output-to-action pipeline into B. Without a downstream action path, cascading error is not supported.
conditions: IF B is wired to consume A’s outputs as authoritative inputs, reassess.
IF B gains action-taking tools or automation hooks, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before any handoff from A to B.
Add validation checks on any A-generated text.
Keep B’s action tools disabled unless needed.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source projects with no data classes touched and no permissions requested, so there is no documented residency or regulated-data mismatch. The remaining issue is documentation uncertainty: agent B is unverified while agent A is verified, so compliance posture is less certain but not evidence of a breach.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data classes, reassess compliance.
IF deployment introduces retention or residency requirements, verify them explicitly.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Record data residency and retention settings before deployment.
Recheck compliance if either repo changes handling of user data.
